en: Udāna 6.5 The Second Discourse on Various Non-Buddhist Teachers Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, many ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of various sects were staying at Sāvatthī, holding diverse views, diverse convictions, diverse inclinations, and relying on diverse doctrinal positions.
Among them, some ascetics and brahmins held such a doctrine and such a view:
“The self and the world are eternal; this alone is true, all else is false.
Yet there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“The self and the world are non-eternal; this alone is true, all else is false.”
There are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
"The self and the world are both eternal and non-eternal; this alone is the truth, all else is vain.
Furthermore, there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Neither eternal nor non-eternal are the self and the world; this alone is the truth, all else is vain.
There are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“The self and the world are created by oneself; this alone is the truth, all else is vain.”
There are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
"The self and the world are created by another; this alone is true, all else is false.
There are some other recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Both self-made and other-made; both the self and the world: this alone is true, all else is false.
Yet there are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Neither self-made nor other-made; arisen by chance, both the self and the world: this alone is true, all else is false.”
There are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain, the self and the world, are eternal; this alone is true, all else is false.
Yet there are other recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain, the self, and the world are finite; this alone is true, all else is false.
There are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain, the self, and the world are both finite and infinite; this alone is true, all else is false.”
There are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Neither eternal nor non-eternal are pleasure and pain, the self, and the world; this alone is true, all else is false.
There are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain are self-made; both the self and the world are [self-made]. This alone is the truth, all else is vain.
Yet there are some ascetics and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain are made by another; both the self and the world are made by another. This alone is the truth, all else is vain.”
There are some recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain are both self-made and made by another; the self and the world are both self-made and made by another; this alone is true, all else is false.
Yet there are other recluses and brahmins who hold such a doctrine and such a view:
“Pleasure and pain are produced neither by oneself nor by another, but arise fortuitously; both the self and the world are thus. This alone is the truth, all else is vain.
Having fallen into quarreling, strife, and dispute, they dwell piercing one another with verbal daggers, saying:
“The Dhamma is like this, it is not like that!”
“Such is the Dhamma, such is the Dhamma.
Then, in the morning, a number of bhikkhus dressed themselves, took their bowls and robes, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.

Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, after their meal, returning from their alms round, they approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

"Here, Bhante, many ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of various sects are residing in Sāvatthī, holding various views, various inclinations, various preferences, and relying on various foundations for their views.
Among them, some ascetics and brahmins are of such speech and such views: [text continues]"
‘The self and the world are eternal; this alone is true, all else is false’ … [and so on] … they live engaged in quarreling, strife, and dispute, stabbing one another with the weapons of the tongue:
‘The Dhamma is thus, it is not thus; the Dhamma is otherwise, it is not otherwise.’
“Such is the Dhamma, such is the Dhamma.
“Bhikkhus, the wanderers of other sects are blind and sightless;
they do not know what is beneficial and they do not know what is harmful; they do not know the Dhamma and they do not know what is contrary to the Dhamma.”

Not knowing what is beneficial and not knowing what is harmful, not knowing what is the Dhamma and not knowing what is non-Dhamma, they live engaged in quarrels, disputes, and arguments, piercing one another with verbal weapons:
“The Dhamma is like this, it is not like that;
the Dhamma is not like this, it is like that.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“It seems that some recluses and brahmins cling to these things.”
They sink in the interval,
without even reaching the mass of darkness.
Thus ends the fifth [sutta].
